correctness.rationale: For an ordered tuple with all products zero the joint image W lies in the common kernel K. On the locus of the two exact ranks the maps to W and K are regular: locally a nonzero maximal minor of the horizontal or vertical concatenation gives the corresponding Grassmannian chart. Recovering the flag from the tuple therefore inverts the incidence-bundle parametrization on the reduced stratum. Its fiber is the open subset of Hom(V/K,W)^ell where the horizontal concatenation is onto and the vertical concatenation is injective. The two rank inequalities are necessary and sufficient: for a≥b use an injective first map covering b basis vectors of W and the unused slots in the other ell−1 maps to hit the rest; for b≥a use a surjective first map and assign the remaining input vectors to distinct slots in the other maps. This works over every field and handles equality; a single zero rank forces the other to be zero. The flag dimension a(n−a)+b(n−a−b) plus the affine fiber dimension ell·a·b gives the claimed formula. A dense flag chart and the open bundle give rationality, and the nonempty open inherits geometric integrality and smoothness. For counting, simultaneous lattice inversion over allowable target image U and required contained kernel T counts maps from (V/K)/T into U in each term. The two Möbius signs and powers yield exactly the given sum and the flag choice gives the Gaussian prefactor. Transposition exchanges the horizontal and vertical ranks. A clean-room rank-one enumeration and explicit span counting for n=3, ell=2 agrees cell by cell at q=2,3,4, totaling 148, 1665, and 9136 respectively. The zero tuple at n=0 is included; no reducedness claim about the whole scheme is needed.
residual_risks: The independent census uses dimensions where a single square-zero operator has rank at most one; the arbitrary-dimensional result rests on the flag parametrization and inversion, not those finite checks.

originality.rationale: The exact claim has equivalent coverage in distinct indexed records. In particular the joint top–socle census has the same framed objects, feasible pairs, flag-bundle geometry and an algebraically identical point count. The double-flag enumeration explicitly counts a strictly finer profile and taking its marginal yields the frozen coefficient. This is a finding of substantive corpus coverage, not an attribution of historical priority. The compared exact records have later catalogue path dates; those dates are not evidence that the frozen author obtained the mathematics from them or that they were published first. The older primary literature inspected below was not shown to give the exact full profile.
residual_risks: No chronology beyond catalogue path dates or relationship between the equivalent records was established; the verdict concerns verified coverage, not priority.
Historical Hall/quiver counting literature was not exhaustively surveyed.

value.rationale: The theorem addresses a natural family of representation varieties over arbitrary fields. The radical and socle together specify which canonical flag occurs; the exact labeled arithmetic profile, sharp simultaneous feasibility and structure of all reduced strata are informative beyond a rank identity, one field or a component count. This is a judgment of mathematical usefulness of the theorem, not of added originality against the equivalent indexed results.
residual_risks: No conclusions on closure incidence, representation isomorphism classes or the entire representation scheme are derived.
